subtitle: A hostage prince turns borrowed mint and script into the mark of Manikya rule

panels.shot: low-angle dramatic close-up on a single silver coin held between fingers, palace and forest hills blurred behind
panels.action: Ratna Manikya I, older and resolute, holds up a freshly struck coin catching the light, the wooded hills of Tripura and the shadow of a distant Bengal-style minaret behind him.

dialogue.text: From hostage in a sultan’s court to king of the hills, Ratna Manikya I forged Tripura’s fate on small round coins of borrowed silver.

i18n.hi: सुलतान दरबार का बंधक, पहाड़ों का राजा – रत्न माणिक्य प्रथम ने उधारी चाँदी के छोटे गोल सिक्कों पर त्रिपुरा की किस्मत गढ़ी

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Bengal Sultanate hall, with young Ratna in the background among courtiers
panels.action: A youthful Ratna Manikya I stands slightly apart in a grand Bengal Sultanate audience hall, arches soaring above, as Persian-robed officials speak around him.

dialogue.text: The Rajmala remembers a Tripura prince sent to the Bengal Sultan, a hostage and a guest, watching another court’s power with sharp, quiet eyes.

i18n.hi: ‘राजमाला’ कहती है, त्रिपुरा का एक राजकुमार बंगाल के सुलतान के पास भेजा गया – बंधक भी, मेहमान भी – जो चुपचाप दूसरी अदालत की ताकत नापता रहा

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Ratna watching scribes and treasurers at work
panels.action: From behind Ratna Manikya I, we see Bengal scribes at long benches, writing in Persian and Bengali scripts, while treasurers weigh coins on precise balances.

dialogue.text: Here he saw registers in Persian hands, Kayastha scribes bending over ledgers, and silver disks weighed and counted with cold exact care.

i18n.hi: यहाँ उसने फ़ारसी रजिस्टर देखे, कायस्थ लिखाड़ी खाते पर झुके, और ठंडी सटीकता से तोले-गिने जाते चाँदी के चक्के

panels.shot: tight close-up on Ratna’s face half in shadow, eyes reflecting the glint of coins and the map of Tripura
panels.action: Ratna’s face is lit by lamplight, one eye catching the shine of coins on a table, the other turned toward a painted map of hill and river country.

dialogue.speaker: ratna_manikya_i
dialogue.text: If their silver can bind a delta, what will it do in my hills?

i18n.hi: अगर इनकी चाँदी पूरा डेल्टा बाँध सकती है, तो मेरे पहाड़ों में क्या कर सकती है?

panels.shot: wide shot of a forested frontier road as Ratna returns with a small, armed escort
panels.action: Ratna Manikya I rides along a forest road into the Tripura hills, a compact escort in Bengal-style armour behind him, distant bamboo villages watching.

dialogue.text: With support won in the delta plains, the prince rode back toward Tripura, the Rajmala says, no longer a mere son but a claimant, carrying new allies and old grudges.

i18n.hi: डेल्टा की मैदानी मदद जेब में लेकर, राजकुमार लौट पड़ा त्रिपुरा की ओर – ‘राजमाला’ कहती है – अब सिर्फ बेटा नहीं, दावेदार, नई संगत और पुराने हिसाब लिए

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of the Tripura hill stronghold as Ratna’s forces approach its gates
panels.action: The hill-fort of Tripura rises above dense forest as Ratna’s mixed force of hill warriors and Bengal-trained soldiers advances toward its timbered gate.

dialogue.text: The chroniclers do not soften what followed. Ratna seized the fort, drove his father into exile, and bound his brothers in prison to clear the path to the throne.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार इसकी धार नहीं छुपाते – रत्न ने किला छीना, पिता को देश निकाला दिया, भाइयों को बेड़ियों में जकड़ सिंहासन की राह साफ की

panels.shot: medium shot in a dim prison corridor, Ratna framed between barred doors, back to the viewer
panels.action: Seen from behind, Ratna Manikya I walks a narrow stone corridor lined with barred doors, a single torch throwing stark shadows across his rigid shoulders.

dialogue.text: The same Rajmala that praises him as builder names him usurper. In its verses, power in Tripura changes hands not with smooth ritual, but with chains and exile.

i18n.hi: उसी ‘राजमाला’ ने जिसे निर्माता कहा, उसे हड़पने वाला भी लिखा – उसकी पंक्तियों में त्रिपुरा की गद्दी रस्मों से नहीं, ज़ंजीरों और निर्वासन से बदलती है

panels.shot: ceremonial low-angle shot of Ratna on a wooden throne, priests and nobles around
panels.action: Ratna Manikya I sits on a carved wooden throne under a canopy, hill priests and nobles standing in attendance, as a conch-blower announces his kingship.

dialogue.text: Yet from this hard beginning, a long reign took shape. Under Ratna Manikya I, the hill kingdom faced the Bengal Sultanate not as a mere fief, but as a wary neighbour.

i18n.hi: पर इसी कठोर शुरुआत से लंबी हुकूमत गढ़ी गई – रत्न माणिक्य प्रथम के अधीन पहाड़ी राज्य, बंगाल सल्तनत के आगे ज़मींदार नहीं, सतर्क पड़ोसी बन खड़ा हुआ

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of a caravan of families with ox-carts entering the Tripura hills
panels.action: A long line of ox-carts and walking families moves up into the green Tripura hills, with Ratna Manikya I watching from a ridge beside local chiefs.

dialogue.text: Between about 1464 and 1468, the Rajmala speaks of some four thousand Bengali Hindu families brought into Tripura, their carts creaking with tools, icons and scripts.

i18n.hi: लगभग १४६४ से १४६८ के बीच, ‘राजमाला’ कहती है, करीब चार हज़ार बंगाली हिंदू परिवार त्रिपुरा लाए गए – उनकी बैलगाड़ियाँ औज़ारों, मूर्तियों और लिपियों से भरी

panels.shot: medium interior shot of a new administrative hall with Bengali scribes at work
panels.action: Inside a new wooden hall, Kayastha scribes in Bengali dress write on palm leaves and paper, while Ratna Manikya I and a hill chief watch the emerging registers.

dialogue.text: Ratna set these settlers to work. Kayastha ministers rose in his court, bringing Bengali and Persian administrative practice into the hill kingdom’s daily grain and levy.

i18n.hi: रत्न ने इन बसने वालों को काम में जोता – कायस्थ मंत्री उसके दरबार में उभरे, जो बंगाली और फ़ारसी दफ़्तरी तौर-तरीके पहाड़ी राज्य की रोज़मर्रा की लगान-रहन में मिला लाए

panels.shot: close-up on Ratna and a Kayastha minister over a map and tally sticks
panels.action: Ratna Manikya I leans over a rough map with a Kayastha minister, tally sticks and weighted stones marking villages as they plan new assessments.

dialogue.speaker: ratna_manikya_i
dialogue.text: Write their dues, and mine, so none can pretend forgetfulness.

i18n.hi: इनका हक, और मेरा, साफ़ लिखो – ताकि कोई भूल का नाटक न कर सके

panels.shot: evocative side view of an early mint workshop in action
panels.action: In a simple mint workshop, workers hammer blanks on small anvils, while Ratna Manikya I examines a freshly struck coin beside a Bengal-style die-cutter.

dialogue.text: Then came the mint. Modern scholars date his coinage from about 1467, silver and copper disks in Bengal Sultanate fabric and weight, but now bearing Tripura’s own marks.

i18n.hi: फिर आई टकसाल – आधुनिक विद्वान उसके सिक्कों को लगभग १४६७ से मानते हैं – चाँदी-ताँबे के चक्के, कपड़ा और वज़न बंगाल सल्तनत का, निशान अब त्रिपुरा के

panels.shot: macro close-up on the face of a Ratna Manikya coin resting on a wooden table
panels.action: A Ratna Manikya I coin lies on a wooden table, its legends and symbols clearly engraved, Ratna’s hand hovering above as if to claim it.

dialogue.text: His coins spoke in Hindu legends—invoking Vishnu, Shiva, and the Chaturdasha Devata—even as they kept the delta’s tested weights and crisp, circular form.

i18n.hi: उसके सिक्के हिंदू शिलालेखों में बोले – विष्णु, शिव और चतुरदश देवता को पुकारते, पर डेल्टा की परखी तौल और गोल काया बरक़रार रखते

panels.shot: medium shot of Ratna with priests and artisans discussing coin designs
panels.action: Ratna Manikya I sits with a temple priest and a die-engraver, gesturing toward drawings of deities and scripts laid out beside blank planchets.

dialogue.text: In this small space, he bound hill cults and court craft. The names of deities from Tripura’s shrines travelled outward, struck on metal that changed many hands.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं छोटे घेरे में उसने पहाड़ी देव-परंपरा और दरबारी चाल दोनों बाँध दीं – त्रिपुरा के देवस्थानों के नाम धातु पर उकेरे गए, जो हाथ दर हाथ दूर तक चले

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Ratna holding a coin before a shrine of the Chaturdasha Devata
panels.action: In front of a modest hill shrine, Ratna Manikya I lifts a coin as offering, the wooden posts hung with symbols of the Chaturdasha Devata.

dialogue.speaker: ratna_manikya_i
dialogue.text: Let the hills know this metal bears their guardians’ names.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ जान लें – यह धातु उनके रखवालों के नाम ढोती है

panels.shot: medium shot of a merchant weighing Ratna’s coin against a Bengal Sultanate coin in a market
panels.action: In a busy market at the frontier, a bearded merchant carefully balances a Ratna Manikya coin against a Bengal Sultanate coin on his scales, Ratna watching from a shaded corner.

dialogue.text: In weight and feel, his silver matched the delta’s, easing trade. But where the Sultan’s coins bore Islamic invocations, Ratna’s bore Manikya titles and Tripura’s gods.

i18n.hi: वज़न और छुअन में उसकी चाँदी डेल्टा जैसी ही रही – कारोबार आसान हुआ; फर्क बस इतना कि जहाँ सुलतान के सिक्कों पर इस्लामी दुआएँ थीं, रत्न के चक्कों पर माणिक्य उपाधियाँ और त्रिपुरा के देव

panels.shot: close-up on an older Ratna reading or handling one of his own coins thoughtfully
panels.action: An older Ratna Manikya I sits in a quiet chamber, turning one of his early coins between his fingers, deep in thought as the sounds of court life fade behind him.

dialogue.text: Modern numismatists studying these pieces corrected even the Rajmala’s sequence, finding in their dates and styles a clearer calendar of his long, complex rule.

i18n.hi: इन सिक्कों को टटोलते आधुनिक मुद्राशास्त्रियों ने ‘राजमाला’ की कड़ी भी सुधारी – तारीख़ों और ढाल में छिपी तिथियाँ उसके लंबे, उलझे राज की साफ़तर पंचांग बन गईं

panels.shot: museum-style wide shot of a display case at Ujjayanta Palace with Ratna’s coins
panels.action: In the Ujjayanta Palace museum, rows of Ratna Manikya I’s coins lie under glass, a faint reflection of his portrait superimposed in the polished surface.

dialogue.text: Today, in Ujjayanta’s cases, his coins survive where many chronicles fall silent, tiny silver witnesses that the Manikya title predated him, yet shone sharper under his hand.

i18n.hi: आज उज्जयंत के शीशे के केसों में उसके सिक्के वैसे बचे हैं, जैसे न जाने कितनी कथाएँ खो गईं – छोटे चाँदी के गवाह, कि ‘माणिक्य’ उपाधि उससे पहले भी थी, पर उसके हाथों और चमकी

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of a Tripura landscape as coins pass hand to hand in the foreground
panels.action: Over a sweeping view of Tripura’s hills and rivers, a pair of hands in the foreground passes a Ratna Manikya I coin to another, the landscape stretching beyond.

dialogue.text: A prince who rose through exile, harsh in seizure and deft in statecraft, Ratna Manikya I turned borrowed mints and scripts into Tripura’s own voice in metal—a reminder that power often speaks through the smallest things.

i18n.hi: निर्वासन से उठे, कब्ज़े में कठोर, राजकाज में निपुण रत्न माणिक्य प्रथम ने उधारी टकसाल और लिखत को त्रिपुरा की अपनी धातु–आवाज़ बना दिया – याद दिलाते हुए कि ताकत अक्सर सबसे छोटी चीज़ों से बोलती है

title_i18n.en: Ratna Manikya Mints the Ruby Coins
title_i18n.hi: रत्न माणिक्य ने निकाले रूबी सिक्के

subtitle_i18n.en: A hostage prince turns borrowed mint and script into the mark of Manikya rule
subtitle_i18n.hi: बंधक राजकुमार ने उधार टकसाल और लिखत को माणिक्य राज की निशानी बना दिया
